body:
Reviewed head `04bf9758388b` (stacked on #511). The new control is a useful improvement over subtracting the *plain* row from the TLS rows: it keeps the probe atom/fixup/code counts comparable, and the saved probe bytes are restored by lane 0 outside the timed interval, before the synchronization barrier. The previous revision (`dce3365`) passed the 9700X benchmark for all three TLS variants; the new head's 9700X job was still running when checked.

Two validation limitations are noted inline. Neither is evidence that the linker currently produces a wrong binary, but they matter when describing these benchmarks as checking every probe and attributing the delta specifically to TLS relaxation. I would strengthen the oracle before treating the benchmark results as independent correctness evidence for #515.

Follow-up review of `c1a615c91332` (after my review of `04bf975`).

**Previous feedback addressed**
- The local-exec checks now compare each probe's immediate against its own `link->symbols.reference`. Imported initial-exec verifies the first probe's computed GOT slot against an `R_X86_64_TPOFF64` relocation naming `errno` in the written ELF, and requires all remaining probes to reach the same slot. This also covers the single-probe case.
- The deliberately recursive control-mode `CALL` is explicitly documented as dead, link-only code. The benchmark no longer implies these probes are executed to validate program behavior.

**Verification:** The 9700X workflow [run 40491972955](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/actions/runs/40491972955) completed successfully, including **Benchmark the direct path's executables**. The log reports successful target checks for control/general/local/imported at 1, 64, 2,000 and 180,000 workers.

**Non-blocking measurement caveat:** Treat the mode-minus-control numbers as *whole-executable-writer workload deltas*, not isolated TLS relaxation kernel latency. While control and general have equal code bytes, atom and fixup counts, control uses a `PC32` into `.data` versus a `TLSGD` into `.tdata` (the one-worker file sizes are 19,584 vs. 19,592 bytes). Local-dynamic adds a `DTPOFF32` fixup and three code bytes per probe, and imported TLS adds a GOT relocation/dynamic symbol. Recording file sizes, phase timings and counts alongside the deltas in buster-performance will prevent over-attribution.

No new blocking correctness findings in this revision.

Reviewed current head `2d3bdf4adc2a`, including the two documentation-only commits (`cc2fd98`, `2d3bdf4`), the linked [9700X measurement record](https://github.com/buster14a/buster-performance/blob/211db644cd805e92f6c65d90707f6c727f0147b7/docs/measurements/tls-relaxation-515-2026-10-27/README.md), and earlier resolved review threads.

The measured ~19/21/23 ns per access (own general-dynamic / imported general-dynamic / local-dynamic) agrees with the record's 180,000-worker control-subtracted data, and the documentation now explicitly describes these as *whole-writer workload deltas*, not isolated relaxation-instruction latency. The prior probe-target and link-only-control review findings remain addressed. No new C code has been introduced since the successful c1a615c 9700X run.

**Non-blocking reproducibility correction (inline):** the pinned measurement record misstates its sample count. Please correct the source record and update its pinned link if republished. The newest head's 9700X workflow was queued when checked; this head only changes documentation.

Small PR-description nit: the measurement record hyperlink has doubled backticks around its URL (`(\`\`https://...\`\`)`); use a normal Markdown link so readers can navigate to the evidence.

Follow-up review at head `ae7049e59d75` (after review [#5666145099](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/pull/553#pullrequestreview-5666145099)).

**Resolved:** The last P3 reproducibility issue is fixed. The pinned [buster-performance record](https://github.com/buster14a/buster-performance/blob/c5c33148b8d0a891ec7f8eb94faabc748139b3ef/docs/measurements/tls-relaxation-515-2026-10-27/README.md) now specifies 41 timed writes for outputs at or below 4 MiB and 11 for larger outputs, with a separate untimed initial write. The PR description and design doc link to that corrected revision. The prior P2 probe-target verification and P3 link-only-control documentation remain addressed; their review threads are resolved.

**Measurement interpretation:** The published ~19 ns / 21 ns / 23 ns per probe for own GD / imported GD / LD are correctly characterized as *whole-writer* control-subtracted costs, with distinct fixup/section and relocation workloads itemized. The record's raw timings, counts, file sizes, phase decomposition, job references, and limitations support this description.

**Verification:** The last code-changing head `c1a615c` passed the Ryzen 7 9700X executable-benchmark job, including all four probe modes and sizes (1, 64, 2,000, 180,000). The newer commits are documentation-only. At review time, the current head's [9700X run](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/actions/runs/40494643695) was queued, while [Measurement storage](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/actions/runs/40494643675) passed.

**Verdict:** No outstanding review findings or new blocking issues identified. From the reviewed change's correctness and measurement-evidence perspective, this is ready once the required CI checks succeed. No merge performed.
